Frequently Asked Questions

Why does my Berea home’s new thermostat read right while rooms still feel wrong?

Because the thermostat measures one hallway, not the house. Room-level differences trace to duct balance, insulation variation, and load differences that no control fixes alone. A system evaluation identifies where the delivery is failing, and the correction targets ducts or balance rather than another gadget.

Is it worth adding a heat pump to a house that has always run gas heat?

Frequently, and the hybrid option means it is not either-or. A heat pump carries mild weather at lower operating cost while the existing furnace handles cold snaps, switching automatically at the economic point. The comparison gets run with your actual utility rates so the answer is arithmetic.

How do I know if the original wiring in my postwar Berea home is still safe?

Through an evaluation rather than assumption in either direction. Plenty of postwar wiring remains serviceable; the risk hides in overloaded circuits, deteriorated insulation, and amateur additions over the decades. The assessment documents actual condition and ranks any corrections by risk.

What does a whole-home generator cost to run during an outage?

Fuel consumption scales with the load it carries, which is why sizing matters twice. A unit covering essential circuits burns meaningfully less than whole-home coverage running the air conditioner. The estimate includes consumption figures for both tiers so operating cost is part of the decision, not a surprise.

Which nearby communities do your Berea routes reach?

Travelers Rest, Easley, and Taylors connect directly to the same dispatch. The chat team can confirm any western county address.
